PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2031: Prisma needs to perform transactions, which requires your MongoDB server to be run as a replica set.
bugs.root_cause: DATABASE_URL had directConnection=true but was missing replicaSet=rs0. Without the explicit replicaSet param, Prisma's topology discovery is bypassed and it cannot confirm it is talking to a replica set, causing all writes to fail.
bugs.fix: Use replicaSet=rs0 alone — directConnection=true skips the handshake that returns the set name, causing a mismatch. Final URL: mongodb://localhost:27017/chem_app?replicaSet=rs0

bugs.error_message: ReplicaSetNoPrimary / P2031 recurring on Windows Docker Desktop WSL2
bugs.root_cause: replicaSet=rs0 alone opens a persistent RS monitor whose heartbeat connections are reset by the WSL2 NAT proxy. directConnection=true alone gives Prisma a Single topology which triggers P2031 on all writes.
bugs.fix: Use replicaSet=rs0&directConnection=true together. directConnection skips the persistent RS monitor (no dropped heartbeats). replicaSet causes the driver to validate setName from the hello handshake so Prisma sees RS topology and does not throw P2031.

bugs.error_message: ReplicaSetNoPrimary and 'actual name <none>' — root cause: native Windows MongoDB shadowing Docker port
bugs.root_cause: A native mongod.exe Windows service was running on 127.0.0.1:27017. Windows routes specific-bind (127.0.0.1:27017) before Docker's wildcard-bind (0.0.0.0:27017), so every connection hit the standalone Windows MongoDB instead of the Docker RS container. The standalone returns hello with no setName, causing all RS connection attempts to fail.
bugs.fix: Stop and disable the Windows MongoDB service (service name: MongoDB). After that, 127.0.0.1:27017 routes to Docker's port-forwarded RS container and replicaSet=rs0 works correctly.
